description: 1Password relies on open source software every day. It's fair to say that 1Password wouldn't exist without the open source community, so we want to give back and help teams be more productive and secure.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: 1Password for Startups is an official founder perk and enablement program provided by 1Password, designed to assist early-stage software companies and engineering teams building modern technology products. Qualifying ventures receive up to Free 1Password Teams for open source projects in platform credits and operational resources, premium infrastructure access, and operational onboarding.

By eliminating upfront software costs across Security & Compliance, the program enables startup teams to preserve runway while deploying robust, enterprise-ready infrastructure on 1Password's battle-tested platform.

Participating companies benefit from technical onboarding resources, direct guidance from 1Password's solutions engineering specialists, and structured pathways to scale as their commercial customer base expands.

sections.heading: Key focus areas & strategic priorities
paragraphs: The 1Password for Startups is tailored for ventures leveraging 1Password's platform to accelerate product delivery. Core focus areas include:
bullets: Production infrastructure deployment: Running mission-critical workloads, databases, and microservices on 1Password's cloud architecture.
Developer toolchain automation: Implementing CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, and developer environments using 1Password's developer platform.
Enterprise security and observability: Configuring end-to-end encryption, identity controls, and operational telemetry to meet industry compliance standards.
Scalable application architectures: Building and optimizing customer-facing web, mobile, and API-driven interfaces backed by 1Password's global network.

sections.heading: Eligibility, evaluation & review criteria
paragraphs: To qualify for 1Password for Startups, startup candidates must satisfy 1Password's standard program requirements:
bullets: Company stage and structure: Early-stage incorporated legal entity (typically Seed or Series A) with an active product domain and registered corporate identity.
Venture backing or affiliation: Participation in a recognized accelerator, venture fund portfolio, or startup partner network recognized by 1Password.
Product development readiness: A live product in development or production actively integrating 1Password's software tools into its technical stack.
Credit utilization history: First-time recipient status with no prior commercial redemptions of standard startup credits on 1Password's platform.

sections.heading: How to apply & milestone delivery
paragraphs: Eligible startups can apply directly on 1Password's program page at https://github.com/1Password/for-open-source. Complete the verification form with your company details, institutional email address, accelerator or investor affiliation, and technical stack summary.
Applications are evaluated on an open enrollment window (12 months). Decisions and credit provisioning are typically completed within 5 to 10 business days following account validation.
Once admitted, founders gain access to the developer console, onboarding workshops, and dedicated support channels to quickly integrate 1Password's tools into their infrastructure.

description: Ideas → Prompt → Prod TL;DR: The barrier to building software has collapsed. This grant gives you $200 USDG to access a month of the highest tier of AI coding tools so you can build and ship something meaningful on Solana. Approved builders receive 50% upfront and 50% upon shipping.

This grant gives you $200 USDG to access a month of the highest tier of AI coding tools so you can build and ship something meaningful on Solana.
Approved builders receive 50% upfront and 50% upon shipping.
The Hypothesis For the first time, building software is no longer gated by technical skill but by ideas and agency.

sections.heading: Program details
paragraphs: AI coding tools have compressed weeks of work into hours.
The people who win in this environment are the ones who have something they want to build, take initiative, and actually ship.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Ideas → Prompt → Prod TL;DR: The barrier to building software has collapsed. This grant gives you $200 USDG to access a month of the highest tier of AI coding tools so you can build and ship something meaningful on Solana. Approved builders receive 50% upfront and 50% upon shipping. The Hypothesis For the first time, building software is no longer gated by technical skill but by ideas and agency. AI coding tools have compressed weeks of work into hours. The people who win in this environment are the ones who have something they want to build, take initiative, and actually ship. This grant is a small nudge in that direction: give you access to a powerful coding tool at the right moment and help you turn an idea into a shipped Solana product. You get $200 USDG to cover an AI coding Pro subscription. 50% upfront, 50% after you've shipped. The only requirement is that it should be a working Solana product. How It Works Apply on Superteam Earn with a clear description of what you want to build and how you'll use AI tools. If approved, you'll receive 50% of the grant upfront (post KYC; to be done on this page on Earn) in the following weekly payout cycle. Approved KYC and payments are sent for processing on Mondays and paid to you by Friday of the same week. From there, you build and ship. After your product/MVP is live, share your project's URL, GitHub repo, and upload your coding subscription receipt(s) to the tranche application form on this listing — the totals shown in the receipt(s) should be $200. This tranche application form will be visible to you after you have received your first tranche. Upon review and approval, you will receive the leftover 50% of the grant. What We're Looking For The scope in your application form should be clear and practical (read: shippable). Your idea/project should have some Solana integration. A live, working product/MVP at the time of your second tranche application. While open-source repos are encouraged, you may keep your repo private. If you decide to close-source your code, you are required to share access with abhwshek@gmail.com so that we can review the code. Questions? Reach out to support@superteam.fun for help.

name: America's Seed Fund (NSF SBIR / STTR)
description: America’s Seed Fund, powered by the National Science Foundation (NSF SBIR / STTR), awards up to $2,000,000 in non-dilutive federal grants for deep-tech, cryptographic, and computational innovations.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: America's Seed Fund (NSF SBIR / STTR) is a high-impact funding program administered by National Science, dedicated to supporting independent researchers, open-source technologists, and public-interest developers. The initiative deploys non-dilutive funding up to Up to $2,000,000 (Equity-Free) to advance privacy-preserving tools, digital sovereignty, and decentralized protocols.
The program specifically prioritizes open digital infrastructure and software commons that serve global communities without relying on extractive or proprietary business models.
Awardees work alongside seasoned technical mentors and domain experts, receiving sustained milestone funding, governance guidance, and peer review throughout the project lifecycle.

sections.heading: Key focus areas & strategic priorities
paragraphs: Grants from National Science are directed toward projects that reinforce open-access computing and technical transparency. Strategic funding tracks include:
bullets: Open-source protocol development: Publishing audited, permissively licensed (MIT/Apache 2.0) software that advances open internet standards.
Digital privacy and censorship resistance: Creating cryptographic tools and communication protocols that protect individual user sovereignty.
Public goods infrastructure: Maintaining foundational libraries, network clients, and diagnostic tools vital to the decentralized developer community.
Applied cryptographic research: Producing peer-reviewed research, formal proofs, and reference implementations for novel cryptographic primitives.

sections.heading: Eligibility, evaluation & review criteria
paragraphs: Proposals submitted to National Science undergo evaluation against strict open-source and public-utility standards:
bullets: Open licensing standard: 100% of funded code, documentation, and research outputs must be published under recognized open-source licenses.
Technical merit and feasibility: Sound architectural design supported by clear technical specifications and realistic engineering milestones.
Societal and community impact: Direct benefit to civil society, digital rights, independent research, or the broader open-source ecosystem.
Governance and transparency: Transparent project stewardship, regular progress updates, and community-accessible development roadmaps.

sections.heading: How to apply & milestone delivery
paragraphs: Interested teams should review the formal guidelines and submit an application through the official National Science portal at https://seedfund.nsf.gov. Proposals must outline the problem statement, proposed technical implementation, milestone roadmap, budget breakdown, and team background.
Applications follow a rolling intake cadence. Shortlisted applicants undergo technical interviews and peer review before final grant determination.

Funding is released in tranches linked to verifiable deliverables (e.g., initial advance upon award execution, mid-term tranche upon testnet or prototype release, and final tranche upon peer review and public code release).

name: CircleCI Startup Program

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: CircleCI Startup Program is an official founder perk and enablement program provided by CircleCI Startup, designed to assist early-stage software companies and engineering teams building modern technology products. Qualifying ventures receive up to Up to $20,000 in compute credits in platform credits and operational resources, premium infrastructure access, and operational onboarding.

By eliminating upfront software costs across Developer Tools, the program enables startup teams to preserve runway while deploying robust, enterprise-ready infrastructure on CircleCI Startup's battle-tested platform.

Participating companies benefit from technical onboarding resources, direct guidance from CircleCI Startup's solutions engineering specialists, and structured pathways to scale as their commercial customer base expands.

sections.heading: Key focus areas & strategic priorities
paragraphs: The CircleCI Startup Program is tailored for ventures leveraging CircleCI Startup's platform to accelerate product delivery. Core focus areas include:
bullets: Production infrastructure deployment: Running mission-critical workloads, databases, and microservices on CircleCI Startup's cloud architecture.
Developer toolchain automation: Implementing CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, and developer environments using CircleCI Startup's developer platform.
Enterprise security and observability: Configuring end-to-end encryption, identity controls, and operational telemetry to meet industry compliance standards.
Scalable application architectures: Building and optimizing customer-facing web, mobile, and API-driven interfaces backed by CircleCI Startup's global network.

sections.heading: Eligibility, evaluation & review criteria
paragraphs: To qualify for CircleCI Startup Program, startup candidates must satisfy CircleCI Startup's standard program requirements:
bullets: Company stage and structure: Early-stage incorporated legal entity (typically Seed or Series A) with an active product domain and registered corporate identity.
Venture backing or affiliation: Participation in a recognized accelerator, venture fund portfolio, or startup partner network recognized by CircleCI Startup.
Product development readiness: A live product in development or production actively integrating CircleCI Startup's software tools into its technical stack.
Credit utilization history: First-time recipient status with no prior commercial redemptions of standard startup credits on CircleCI Startup's platform.

sections.heading: How to apply & milestone delivery
paragraphs: Eligible startups can apply directly on CircleCI Startup's program page at https://circleci.com/startup-program/. Complete the verification form with your company details, institutional email address, accelerator or investor affiliation, and technical stack summary.
Applications are evaluated on an open enrollment window (24 months). Decisions and credit provisioning are typically completed within 5 to 10 business days following account validation.
Once admitted, founders gain access to the developer console, onboarding workshops, and dedicated support channels to quickly integrate CircleCI Startup's tools into their infrastructure.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Decentralized Cloud Foundation Grants is an ecosystem grant initiative powered by Decentralized Cloud, designed to accelerate the development of critical protocols, developer tooling, and decentralized applications across Decentralized Cloud Foundation. The program provides milestone-based tranches sized according to project scope to empower talented engineering teams building scalable onchain solutions.

Grant capital is focused on high-priority infrastructure and use cases spanning dApp, helping teams move rapidly from prototype to production with direct technical and distribution support from Decentralized Cloud.

Beyond capital, Decentralized Cloud Foundation Grants connects recipients with core network engineers, security auditors, and community stakeholders to ensure smooth mainnet deployment and sustained user adoption.

sections.heading: Key focus areas & strategic priorities
paragraphs: The technical steering committee for Decentralized Cloud Foundation Grants seeks proposals that deliver tangible utility and measurable onchain traction to Decentralized Cloud Foundation. Priority categories include:
bullets: Decentralized protocol engineering: Implementing secure smart contracts, state transition logic, and liquidity protocols tailored to Decentralized Cloud Foundation.
Developer frameworks & SDKs: Building open-source client libraries, testing suites, local testnets, and developer documentation that streamline onboarding.
Data availability & indexing infrastructure: Engineering high-throughput oracles, event indexers, and subgraphs for real-time protocol telemetry.
User-facing applications & interfaces: Launching accessible frontends, decentralized identity integrations, and automated agent workflows for global users.

sections.heading: Eligibility, evaluation & review criteria
paragraphs: Proposals for Decentralized Cloud Foundation Grants are reviewed by core engineers and ecosystem evaluators using four primary criteria:
bullets: Architectural rigor and code quality: Well-structured GitHub repositories featuring clean commit histories, modular contracts, and comprehensive unit tests.
Clear ecosystem alignment: A focused value proposition that solves tangible technical bottlenecks or drives sustained transaction activity on Decentralized Cloud Foundation.
Team capability: Proven track record in software engineering, cryptography, or distributed systems capable of shipping complex deliverables on schedule.
Milestone feasibility: A well-defined work breakdown structure with concrete, verifiable acceptance criteria for each development sprint.

sections.heading: How to apply & milestone delivery
paragraphs: Founders and engineering teams can initiate their proposal via the official Decentralized Cloud Foundation Grants portal at https://wiki.crust.network/docs/en/crustGrants. Submissions must include an architectural overview, link to public or private repositories, deliverable milestones, and budget allocation breakdown.

Applications are reviewed on a rolling intake cadence. Shortlisted teams participate in a technical discovery interview with Decentralized Cloud's engineering committee to refine project milestones and security specifications.

Disbursements are milestone-gated: an initial tranche (25-30%) is provided upon onboarding, followed by milestone releases upon testnet deployment, successful smart contract audits, and production mainnet launch.

name: Deel for Startups
description: Deel for Startups provides fast-growing teams with 5 free contractor seats for life and 20% to 50% discounts on international payroll, employer of record (EOR), and immigration support.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Deel for Startups is an official founder perk and enablement program provided by Deel, designed to assist early-stage software companies and engineering teams building modern technology products. Qualifying ventures receive up to 5 seats free for life + 12-month discounts in platform credits and operational resources, premium infrastructure access, and operational onboarding.

By eliminating upfront software costs across HR & Payroll, the program enables startup teams to preserve runway while deploying robust, enterprise-ready infrastructure on Deel's battle-tested platform.

Participating companies benefit from technical onboarding resources, direct guidance from Deel's solutions engineering specialists, and structured pathways to scale as their commercial customer base expands.

sections.heading: Key focus areas & strategic priorities
paragraphs: The Deel for Startups is tailored for ventures leveraging Deel's platform to accelerate product delivery. Core focus areas include:
bullets: Production infrastructure deployment: Running mission-critical workloads, databases, and microservices on Deel's cloud architecture.
Developer toolchain automation: Implementing CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, and developer environments using Deel's developer platform.
Enterprise security and observability: Configuring end-to-end encryption, identity controls, and operational telemetry to meet industry compliance standards.
Scalable application architectures: Building and optimizing customer-facing web, mobile, and API-driven interfaces backed by Deel's global network.

sections.heading: Eligibility, evaluation & review criteria
paragraphs: To qualify for Deel for Startups, startup candidates must satisfy Deel's standard program requirements:
bullets: Company stage and structure: Early-stage incorporated legal entity (typically Seed or Series A) with an active product domain and registered corporate identity.
Venture backing or affiliation: Participation in a recognized accelerator, venture fund portfolio, or startup partner network recognized by Deel.
Product development readiness: A live product in development or production actively integrating Deel's software tools into its technical stack.
Credit utilization history: First-time recipient status with no prior commercial redemptions of standard startup credits on Deel's platform.

sections.heading: How to apply & milestone delivery
paragraphs: Eligible startups can apply directly on Deel's program page at https://www.deel.com/segments/startups/. Complete the verification form with your company details, institutional email address, accelerator or investor affiliation, and technical stack summary.
Applications are evaluated on an open enrollment window (12 months). Decisions and credit provisioning are typically completed within 5 to 10 business days following account validation.
Once admitted, founders gain access to the developer console, onboarding workshops, and dedicated support channels to quickly integrate Deel's tools into their infrastructure.

name: EIC Accelerator (European Innovation Council)
description: Flagship EU funding program supporting breakthrough deep-tech startups and SMEs with blended finance (non-dilutive grant + direct equity).

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: EIC Accelerator (European Innovation Council) is a high-impact funding program administered by European Commission, dedicated to supporting independent researchers, open-source technologists, and public-interest developers. The initiative deploys non-dilutive funding up to Up to €2.5M Grant + €15M Equity to advance privacy-preserving tools, digital sovereignty, and decentralized protocols.
The program specifically prioritizes open digital infrastructure and software commons that serve global communities without relying on extractive or proprietary business models.
Awardees work alongside seasoned technical mentors and domain experts, receiving sustained milestone funding, governance guidance, and peer review throughout the project lifecycle.

sections.heading: Key focus areas & strategic priorities
paragraphs: Grants from European Commission are directed toward projects that reinforce open-access computing and technical transparency. Strategic funding tracks include:
bullets: Open-source protocol development: Publishing audited, permissively licensed (MIT/Apache 2.0) software that advances open internet standards.
Digital privacy and censorship resistance: Creating cryptographic tools and communication protocols that protect individual user sovereignty.
Public goods infrastructure: Maintaining foundational libraries, network clients, and diagnostic tools vital to the decentralized developer community.
Applied cryptographic research: Producing peer-reviewed research, formal proofs, and reference implementations for novel cryptographic primitives.

sections.heading: Eligibility, evaluation & review criteria

name: Mozilla Foundation Awards & Fellowships
description: The Mozilla Foundation Awards & Fellowships program provides funding between $10,000 and $100,000+ for researchers, open-source developers, and civil society leaders building a healthier internet.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Mozilla Foundation Awards & Fellowships is a high-impact funding program administered by Mozilla, dedicated to supporting independent researchers, open-source technologists, and public-interest developers. The initiative deploys non-dilutive funding up to $10,000 - $100,000+ to advance privacy-preserving tools, digital sovereignty, and decentralized protocols.
The program specifically prioritizes open digital infrastructure and software commons that serve global communities without relying on extractive or proprietary business models.
Awardees work alongside seasoned technical mentors and domain experts, receiving sustained milestone funding, governance guidance, and peer review throughout the project lifecycle.

sections.heading: Key focus areas & strategic priorities
paragraphs: Grants from Mozilla are directed toward projects that reinforce open-access computing and technical transparency. Strategic funding tracks include:
bullets: Open-source protocol development: Publishing audited, permissively licensed (MIT/Apache 2.0) software that advances open internet standards.
Digital privacy and censorship resistance: Creating cryptographic tools and communication protocols that protect individual user sovereignty.
Public goods infrastructure: Maintaining foundational libraries, network clients, and diagnostic tools vital to the decentralized developer community.
Applied cryptographic research: Producing peer-reviewed research, formal proofs, and reference implementations for novel cryptographic primitives.

sections.heading: Eligibility, evaluation & review criteria
paragraphs: Proposals submitted to Mozilla undergo evaluation against strict open-source and public-utility standards:
bullets: Open licensing standard: 100% of funded code, documentation, and research outputs must be published under recognized open-source licenses.
Technical merit and feasibility: Sound architectural design supported by clear technical specifications and realistic engineering milestones.
Societal and community impact: Direct benefit to civil society, digital rights, independent research, or the broader open-source ecosystem.
Governance and transparency: Transparent project stewardship, regular progress updates, and community-accessible development roadmaps.

sections.heading: How to apply & milestone delivery
paragraphs: Interested teams should review the formal guidelines and submit an application through the official Mozilla portal at https://www.mozillafoundation.org/en/what-we-do/grantmaking/. Proposals must outline the problem statement, proposed technical implementation, milestone roadmap, budget breakdown, and team background.
Applications follow scheduled review cycles (Periodic RFP Calls). Shortlisted applicants undergo technical interviews and peer review before final grant determination.

Funding is released in tranches linked to verifiable deliverables (e.g., initial advance upon award execution, mid-term tranche upon testnet or prototype release, and final tranche upon peer review and public code release).

sections.heading: Key focus areas & strategic priorities

sections.heading: Eligibility, evaluation & review criteria

sections.heading: How to apply & milestone delivery

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Prototype Fund is a high-impact funding program administered by Open Knowledge Germany, dedicated to supporting independent researchers, open-source technologists, and public-interest developers. Awardees work alongside seasoned technical mentors and domain experts, receiving sustained milestone funding, governance guidance, and peer review throughout the project lifecycle.

sections.heading: Key focus areas & strategic priorities
paragraphs: Grants from Open Knowledge Germany are directed toward projects that reinforce open-access computing and technical transparency. Strategic funding tracks include:
bullets: Open-source protocol development: Publishing audited, permissively licensed (MIT/Apache 2.0) software that advances open internet standards.
Digital privacy and censorship resistance: Creating cryptographic tools and communication protocols that protect individual user sovereignty.
Public goods infrastructure: Maintaining foundational libraries, network clients, and diagnostic tools vital to the decentralized developer community.
Applied cryptographic research: Producing peer-reviewed research, formal proofs, and reference implementations for novel cryptographic primitives.

sections.heading: Eligibility, evaluation & review criteria
paragraphs: Proposals submitted to Open Knowledge Germany undergo evaluation against strict open-source and public-utility standards:
bullets: Open licensing standard: 100% of funded code, documentation, and research outputs must be published under recognized open-source licenses.
Technical merit and feasibility: Sound architectural design supported by clear technical specifications and realistic engineering milestones.
Societal and community impact: Direct benefit to civil society, digital rights, independent research, or the broader open-source ecosystem.
Governance and transparency: Transparent project stewardship, regular progress updates, and community-accessible development roadmaps.

sections.heading: How to apply & milestone delivery
paragraphs: Interested teams should review the formal guidelines and submit an application through the official Open Knowledge Germany portal at https://www.prototypefund.de/en/. Proposals must outline the problem statement, proposed technical implementation, milestone roadmap, budget breakdown, and team background.
Applications follow scheduled review cycles (Biannual Rounds). Shortlisted applicants undergo technical interviews and peer review before final grant determination.

Funding is released in tranches linked to verifiable deliverables (e.g., initial advance upon award execution, mid-term tranche upon testnet or prototype release, and final tranche upon peer review and public code release).

name: Sovereign Tech Fund (STF)
provider: German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs
description: The Sovereign Tech Fund (STF) provides €50,000 to €500,000+ in non-dilutive open-source funding to maintain and fortify critical digital infrastructure, open protocols, and security libraries.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Sovereign Tech Fund (STF) is a high-impact funding program administered by German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs, dedicated to supporting independent researchers, open-source technologists, and public-interest developers. The initiative deploys non-dilutive funding up to €50,000 - €500,000+ to advance privacy-preserving tools, digital sovereignty, and decentralized protocols.
The program specifically prioritizes open digital infrastructure and software commons that serve global communities without relying on extractive or proprietary business models.
Awardees work alongside seasoned technical mentors and domain experts, receiving sustained milestone funding, governance guidance, and peer review throughout the project lifecycle.

sections.heading: Key focus areas & strategic priorities
paragraphs: Grants from German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs are directed toward projects that reinforce open-access computing and technical transparency. Strategic funding tracks include:
bullets: Open-source protocol development: Publishing audited, permissively licensed (MIT/Apache 2.0) software that advances open internet standards.
Digital privacy and censorship resistance: Creating cryptographic tools and communication protocols that protect individual user sovereignty.
Public goods infrastructure: Maintaining foundational libraries, network clients, and diagnostic tools vital to the decentralized developer community.
Applied cryptographic research: Producing peer-reviewed research, formal proofs, and reference implementations for novel cryptographic primitives.

sections.heading: Eligibility, evaluation & review criteria
paragraphs: Proposals submitted to German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs undergo evaluation against strict open-source and public-utility standards:
bullets: Open licensing standard: 100% of funded code, documentation, and research outputs must be published under recognized open-source licenses.
Technical merit and feasibility: Sound architectural design supported by clear technical specifications and realistic engineering milestones.
Societal and community impact: Direct benefit to civil society, digital rights, independent research, or the broader open-source ecosystem.
Governance and transparency: Transparent project stewardship, regular progress updates, and community-accessible development roadmaps.

sections.heading: How to apply & milestone delivery
paragraphs: Interested teams should review the formal guidelines and submit an application through the official German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs portal at https://www.sovereign.tech/. Proposals must outline the problem statement, proposed technical implementation, milestone roadmap, budget breakdown, and team background.
Applications follow scheduled review cycles (Contribute & Round based). Shortlisted applicants undergo technical interviews and peer review before final grant determination.

Funding is released in tranches linked to verifiable deliverables (e.g., initial advance upon award execution, mid-term tranche upon testnet or prototype release, and final tranche upon peer review and public code release).

sections.heading: Program details

What does this mean for your integration?

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Get up to $10,000 in DD.xyz API credits to add an extra layer of due diligence to your dApp Integrate Webacy's robust APIs to equip you and your users with the critical intelligence needed for effective due diligence and decentralized decision-making within the web3 ecosystem. Empower them with the tools to navigate the landscape confidently and make informed choices. Webacy's Risk Engine is at the core of all out API endpoints. This powerful engine provides the broadest coverage across the blockchain ecosystem by aggregating data from over 15 diverse data providers, complemented by our proprietary data analytics and advanced algorithms. We process millions of signals monthly, incorporating the latest and most up-to-date information spanning compliance, regulatory data, potential threats, and community-sourced insights. What does this mean for your integration? By utilizing DD.xys’ APIs, you provide your users with access to the most extensive and current risk-related data available. Unlike solutions relying on a single data source, our multi-provider approach offers a comprehensive and nuanced understanding of the complexities within web3. Our engine combines the power of AI-driven analysis with human refinement, ensuring both efficient processing and highly accurate information for user evaluation. Facilitating informed decision-making requires providing relevant data across the web3 journey. Our APIs deliver crucial insights at key interaction points: Wallet Risk Insights: Enable users to understand the risk profiles associated with different wallets and their activities. Transaction Intelligence: Provide users with data to evaluate the potential risks associated with specific transactions. Token Analysis: Equip users with comprehensive data and risk assessments for all tokens Smart Contract Analysis: Offer users information to assess the security and potential risks of interacting with various smart contracts. Contextual Awareness: Equip users with the information needed to understand the broader context surrounding their web3 interactions. The DD.xyz Platform is architected to empower projects and end-users throughout their web3 experience. Our APIs are designed to be valuable at every stage, providing the data necessary for individuals to conduct their own due diligence and make well-informed decisions. Built by a team with deep expertise in crypto, cybersecurity, AI, and data integration, Webacy provides the foundational data layer for informed participation in web3. We process vast amounts of information, allowing your users to access critical intelligence and exercise greater autonomy in their web3 journey. Integrate our infrastructure and empower your users with the knowledge they need to navigate web3 with confidence. ️ Apply for the grant now. We are receiving a large volume of applications, and may not have the time to give detailed feedback on every submission. Please keep that in mind before you apply. 🏻‍ Our APIs Threat Risks API This API discovers the risk of any on-chain address. This includes any contract, wallet, EOA (Externally Owned Account), token, NFT, or otherwise. It analyzes an address' threat to others. It returns risk data associated with the supplied address. It flags if the address appears in any sanctioned databases or has been historically flagged as malicious. Some common use cases for this endpoint include: Filtering addresses for spam/sybil Blocking high-risk addresses from utilizing your service (compliance, platform safety) Flagging high-risk addresses (tokens, contracts, P2P participants) Example implementation: Block, limit and/or track unwanted addresses (like spam, bots, clones, OFAC/SCAM/Blacklisted/Terrorism financing addresses) from entering/signing in to your platform. Highlighting token risk analysis prior to a swap, or within a users wallet. Approval Risks API This API analyzes the risks associated with token approvals given by a specific address. It returns data indicating potentially risky approvals, such as those granting unlimited allowance to suspicious contracts. This helps users understand and manage their token permissions. Some common use cases for this endpoint include: Alerting users about potentially dangerous token approvals Providing insights into a user's approval history Identifying and mitigating risks related to token drain attacks Example implementation: Display historical risk data to a user. Better understand a user’s behavioral patterns. Provide recommendations to users based on transactional health history. Assess a user’s historical activity in order to approve or adjust a loan or financial terms. Transaction Risks API This API returns risk data associated with a given transaction. It incorporates various risk factors, including the risk profiles of the involved addresses (both sender and receiver) and the risk associated with the smart contract being interacted with. Some common use cases for this endpoint include: Evaluating the risk level of transactions occurring on your platform Providing users with risk assessments before they confirm transactions Implementing fraud detection mechanisms Example implementation: Exposure Risk API This API returns the 'risk profile' of a given address. It indicates the level of exposure the address has to risky activities based on its historical transactions, on-chain behavior, and the risk profiles of the assets it holds. Some common use cases for this endpoint include: Understanding the overall risk level of a user's wallet Identifying users with high exposure to risky entities or activities Tailoring risk mitigation strategies based on a user's exposure profile Example implementation: Add an UI element so once the user connects their wallet, they’ll be able to see how safe it is (low/medium/safe/safest) directly in your dApp. For example, an infographic “Safety Score: LOW”. Contract Risk API This API analyzes the risk associated with a given smart contract address. It returns data points and risk scores related to the contract's security, potential vulnerabilities, and historical behavior. Some common use cases for this endpoint include: Evaluating the safety of smart contracts before interacting with them Providing users with risk assessments of smart contracts Identifying potentially malicious or vulnerable contracts Identifying past behaviour of contract deployer Example Implementation: Flag tokens, NFTs, NFT collections or addresses in your platform with an UI element in the case they are malicious. Let your users know that the address might be malicious and that they should DYOR. We’ve seen the most demand coming from exchanges, swaps, bridges, DeFi protocols and launchpads. URL Risk This API analyzes the safety of a given URL. It determines if the URL is associated with phishing scams, malware distribution, or other malicious activities. Some common use cases for this endpoint include: Protecting users from phishing attacks by identifying malicious URLs Scanning URLs before allowing users to navigate to them within your application Identifying and blocking known malicious websites Common use case: Quest and SocialFi platforms integrate URL Risk API to check/block/track/limit if any URL/link their users post is malicious/drainer/phishing. Holder Analysis API (Invite Only Endpoint) This API provides detailed analysis of the early holders of a specific token. It returns data points related to the distribution of the token among early adopters, identifying potential risks associated with concentrated ownership or suspicious early activity. Some common use cases for this endpoint include: Conducting due diligence on new tokens Identifying potential risks related to token distribution Providing insights into the early dynamics of a token's ownership Example implementation: AI Agents or trading bots highlighting high bundling or sniping as an issue and not interacting with a potential rug-pull. Highlighting bundling/sniping history prior to a swap.  ️ How it works Submit the application form (won’t take more than 10 minutes!). Wait for 72 hours to hear back with a decision. If approved, you'll receive an email notification for onboarding and further steps.  Guidelines Be concise & precise: Being clear and concise is always helpful. Bonus points if the application contains well-defined technical details (wherever required). Don’t hesitate to contact us to amend or edit your requirements: Beyond what is specified, if you have any unique insight regarding what your current needs are, feel free to reach out to us info@webacy.com.  Do your homework: Read our API docs, research about Webacy and ask questions if needed. Differentiation: Your application should make it clear how your project is differentiated from other similar projects across relevant ecosystems. Frequently asked questions Where can I read more information about Webacy and its APIs? You can access more information at  https://docs.webacy.com/   What chains do you support? We support Solana, Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism, BSC, Sei, Sui, Stellar, Ton, and Base. More on the roadmap How much time do I have to integrate?  You have up to 3 months to integrate but the integration agreement should be signed as soon as you are selected as grant winner. Are there any other benefits? Yes, amongst other benefits are co-marketing (access to an audience of over 250,000 unique users) and Webacy PRO access passes for your community or users. Can I whitelabel the frontend UI of the integration? Yes, you can choose whether to add DD.xyz logo/name, or make it completely yours. We can also provide you with a JavaScript snippet which you can copy and paste for the frontend UI. Who is eligible to apply for the grant? Any dApp that supports and is building on Solana, Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism, BSC, Sei, Ton and Base What criteria will the panelists use to evaluate grants? We prefer projects that 1) yield results quickly 2) are executable by the proposing team. What conditions apply? The only condition is that you periodically update us about the API integration stage and you actively communicate. Will I receive feedback on my proposal if it is rejected? To the best of our abilities given the large volume of submissions.  ️ Apply for the grant now.

sections.heading: Eligibility, evaluation & review criteria

bullets: Architectural rigor and code quality: Well-structured GitHub repositories featuring clean commit histories, modular contracts, and comprehensive unit tests.

Team capability: Proven track record in software engineering, cryptography, or distributed systems capable of shipping complex deliverables on schedule.
Milestone feasibility: A well-defined work breakdown structure with concrete, verifiable acceptance criteria for each development sprint.

sections.heading: How to apply & milestone delivery

Disbursements are milestone-gated: an initial tranche (25-30%) is provided upon onboarding, followed by milestone releases upon testnet deployment, successful smart contract audits, and production mainnet launch.

name: Stripe Atlas
description: Stripe Atlas helps international and domestic founders form a Delaware C-Corporation, obtain a US IRS tax ID (EIN), issue founder shares, and access $2,500 in fee-free payment credits.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Stripe Atlas is an official founder perk and enablement program provided by Stripe Atlas, designed to assist early-stage software companies and engineering teams building modern technology products. Qualifying ventures receive up to $2,500 Stripe credits + $50,000+ in partner perks in platform credits and operational resources, premium infrastructure access, and operational onboarding.

By eliminating upfront software costs across Incorporation & Legal, the program enables startup teams to preserve runway while deploying robust, enterprise-ready infrastructure on Stripe Atlas's battle-tested platform.

Participating companies benefit from technical onboarding resources, direct guidance from Stripe Atlas's solutions engineering specialists, and structured pathways to scale as their commercial customer base expands.

sections.heading: Key focus areas & strategic priorities
paragraphs: The Stripe Atlas is tailored for ventures leveraging Stripe Atlas's platform to accelerate product delivery. Core focus areas include:
bullets: Production infrastructure deployment: Running mission-critical workloads, databases, and microservices on Stripe Atlas's cloud architecture.
Developer toolchain automation: Implementing CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, and developer environments using Stripe Atlas's developer platform.
Enterprise security and observability: Configuring end-to-end encryption, identity controls, and operational telemetry to meet industry compliance standards.
Scalable application architectures: Building and optimizing customer-facing web, mobile, and API-driven interfaces backed by Stripe Atlas's global network.

sections.heading: Eligibility, evaluation & review criteria
paragraphs: To qualify for Stripe Atlas, startup candidates must satisfy Stripe Atlas's standard program requirements:
bullets: Company stage and structure: Early-stage incorporated legal entity (typically Seed or Series A) with an active product domain and registered corporate identity.
Venture backing or affiliation: Participation in a recognized accelerator, venture fund portfolio, or startup partner network recognized by Stripe Atlas.
Product development readiness: A live product in development or production actively integrating Stripe Atlas's software tools into its technical stack.
Credit utilization history: First-time recipient status with no prior commercial redemptions of standard startup credits on Stripe Atlas's platform.

sections.heading: How to apply & milestone delivery
paragraphs: Eligible startups can apply directly on Stripe Atlas's program page at https://stripe.com/in/atlas. Complete the verification form with your company details, institutional email address, accelerator or investor affiliation, and technical stack summary.
Applications are evaluated on an open enrollment window (12 months). Decisions and credit provisioning are typically completed within 5 to 10 business days following account validation.
Once admitted, founders gain access to the developer console, onboarding workshops, and dedicated support channels to quickly integrate Stripe Atlas's tools into their infrastructure.

sections.heading: Program overview

Participating companies benefit from technical onboarding resources, direct guidance from Tally's solutions engineering specialists, and structured pathways to scale as their commercial customer base expands.

sections.heading: Key focus areas & strategic priorities

Scalable application architectures: Building and optimizing customer-facing web, mobile, and API-driven interfaces backed by Tally's global network.

sections.heading: Eligibility, evaluation & review criteria
paragraphs: To qualify for Tally for Startups, startup candidates must satisfy Tally's standard program requirements:
bullets: Company stage and structure: Early-stage incorporated legal entity (typically Seed or Series A) with an active product domain and registered corporate identity.
Venture backing or affiliation: Participation in a recognized accelerator, venture fund portfolio, or startup partner network recognized by Tally.
Product development readiness: A live product in development or production actively integrating Tally's software tools into its technical stack.
Credit utilization history: First-time recipient status with no prior commercial redemptions of standard startup credits on Tally's platform.

sections.heading: How to apply & milestone delivery
paragraphs: Eligible startups can apply directly on Tally's program page at https://tally.so/help/tally-for-startups. Complete the verification form with your company details, institutional email address, accelerator or investor affiliation, and technical stack summary.
Applications are evaluated on an open enrollment window (12 months). Decisions and credit provisioning are typically completed within 5 to 10 business days following account validation.
Once admitted, founders gain access to the developer console, onboarding workshops, and dedicated support channels to quickly integrate Tally's tools into their infrastructure.

name: Thiel Fellowship
description: A two-year, $100,000 grant given to 20-25 young founders and researchers under 22 who want to build new things instead of sitting in a classroom.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Thiel Fellowship is a high-impact funding program administered by Thiel, dedicated to supporting independent researchers, open-source technologists, and public-interest developers. The initiative deploys non-dilutive funding up to $100,000 (No Equity) to advance privacy-preserving tools, digital sovereignty, and decentralized protocols.
The program specifically prioritizes open digital infrastructure and software commons that serve global communities without relying on extractive or proprietary business models.
Awardees work alongside seasoned technical mentors and domain experts, receiving sustained milestone funding, governance guidance, and peer review throughout the project lifecycle.

sections.heading: Key focus areas & strategic priorities
paragraphs: Grants from Thiel are directed toward projects that reinforce open-access computing and technical transparency. Strategic funding tracks include:
bullets: Open-source protocol development: Publishing audited, permissively licensed (MIT/Apache 2.0) software that advances open internet standards.
Digital privacy and censorship resistance: Creating cryptographic tools and communication protocols that protect individual user sovereignty.
Public goods infrastructure: Maintaining foundational libraries, network clients, and diagnostic tools vital to the decentralized developer community.
Applied cryptographic research: Producing peer-reviewed research, formal proofs, and reference implementations for novel cryptographic primitives.

sections.heading: Eligibility, evaluation & review criteria
paragraphs: Proposals submitted to Thiel undergo evaluation against strict open-source and public-utility standards:
bullets: Open licensing standard: 100% of funded code, documentation, and research outputs must be published under recognized open-source licenses.
Technical merit and feasibility: Sound architectural design supported by clear technical specifications and realistic engineering milestones.
Societal and community impact: Direct benefit to civil society, digital rights, independent research, or the broader open-source ecosystem.
Governance and transparency: Transparent project stewardship, regular progress updates, and community-accessible development roadmaps.

sections.heading: How to apply & milestone delivery
paragraphs: Interested teams should review the formal guidelines and submit an application through the official Thiel portal at https://thielfellowship.org. Proposals must outline the problem statement, proposed technical implementation, milestone roadmap, budget breakdown, and team background.
Applications follow a rolling intake cadence. Shortlisted applicants undergo technical interviews and peer review before final grant determination.

Funding is released in tranches linked to verifiable deliverables (e.g., initial advance upon award execution, mid-term tranche upon testnet or prototype release, and final tranche upon peer review and public code release).

description: Audiences Post, Communities Host TL;DR: All our feeds are cooked and touching grass with friends is the final defense. Get up to $500 USDG to cover expenses for organizing Solana & Superteam adjacent meet-ups in your city, as per the guidelines below.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Audiences Post, Communities Host TL;DR: All our feeds are cooked and touching grass with friends is the final defense.
The Superteam touching grass fund is here to support members who host, not just post.

Social media platforms are no longer social.

sections.heading: Program details
paragraphs: By default, you don't see content from your friends, family, or people you're connected with.

Instead, our feeds are dominated by sophisticated professionals who are engineering content to elicit a dopamine response while competing for max share of our attention that they can then package and sell to sponsors.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs:
Audiences Post, Communities Host TL;DR: All our feeds are cooked and touching grass with friends is the final defense.
The Superteam touching grass fund is here to support members who host, not just post.
Get up to $500 USDG to cover expenses for organizing Solana & Superteam adjacent meet-ups in your city, as per the guidelines below.
Social media platforms are no longer social.
By default, you don't see content from your friends, family, or people you're connected with.
Instead, our feeds are dominated by sophisticated professionals who are engineering content to elicit a dopamine response while competing for max share of our attention that they can then package and sell to sponsors.
In such times, IRL events are the last defense to compete with brainrot.
Audiences post, communities host: A big focus for each Superteam is to be the frontier onboarding vehicle for the most promising talent in their local markets.
However, the magic happens when members go from sharing memes in a group chat to forming teams on Solana, and often forge lifelong friendships in the process.
The optimal way to participate in Superteam is to use the access & trust from being a member to find your niche interest and the people you can collaborate with to create weekend projects, products, or companies around it.
Those who do it right will find themselves in more group chats than they can count, spontaneously joining Zoom calls and taking cabs/trains/planes to meet their internet friends.
More on this idea in a previous blog post here.
Therefore, Superteam now supports the Solana Foundation community grants program and recommends applicants with the ability to galvanize the community with in-person events for community grants.
Members are encouraged to host casual events like coffee mixers, dinners, paddle or pickleball tournaments, turf football or cricket, or more structured events like learning groups, weekend hackathons, bounty hunting, or co-working sessions.
As long as you're doing something that (a) brings the Solana community closer together and (b) onboards those on the sidelines into crypto, feel free to apply.
Currently, only Superteam members can be hosts, but anyone can attend.
If this format works, we will drop the host restriction and open it up to anyone in the Superteam ecosystem. Events Playbook The meetups are supposed to be a lot of fun, but it's not all there is to a valuable meetup.
To have a higher chance of success—and to get more from the touching grass fund down the line—we recommend doing as many of these as possible: Limited attendees: Invite a small group of not more than 8–10 people.
Focus on a size and venue that enables everyone to talk to everyone else at least once.
A generic meetup isn't the best fit for this; we're only looking to support meetups where attendees are: developers, operators (marketing, product, ops), creators (writers, researchers, YouTubers, etc.), investors (both angels and VCs), founders, and capital markets professionals.
Primer on crypto: Depending on how much is necessary, help folks find their way into the Superteam and Solana ecosystem.
Make them feel at home!
Merch (optional): Coordinate with your local Superteam team to get merch—T-shirts, stickers, bags, etc.—for attendees to take back as a souvenir.
Food & Coffee: If this is part of your event, an ideal meal is one where (1) everyone can talk to each other, and (2) it's reasonably priced and prudently ordered without wasting food or money.
Onboarding: If you're inviting people who are new to crypto or Solana, ideally you should also act as their buddy & help them find their pathway to contribution via bounties, gigs, jobs, hackathons, asset onboarding/distribution, etc.
Proof of meet-up: Ideally, take pictures and put them up on your social media of choice with a short caption sharing your experience, learnings, or thoughts.
Tag your local Superteam as they might share it as well!
This way you can stay in touch and help make more plans that were discussed at dinner!
What this grant is not for: Events that are purely social or personal with no direct link to Solana or Superteam goals.
Misuse of funds or falsified reports can potentially result in being purged from the Superteam membership. ️ How It Works Create a private event page on Luma.
Please ensure you've added an appropriate title, cover image, and a full description of the event — including the format of the event, schedule if any, who the event is for, outcomes for the event, etc.
Make a grant application for it here on Earn, and include the private Luma link of your event in the application.
Sponsors will usually reply within ~7 days.
If approved, you'll receive a confirmation email.
Once approved: Submit your event to the  Superteam Calendar  so it's visible to the broader community.
You'll receive 50% of the grant upfront (post KYC; to be done on this page on Earn) in the following weekly payout cycle.
Approved KYC and payments are sent for processing on Mondays and paid to you by Friday of the same week.
After the event, upload photos from the event + scanned copies of expense receipts from the event to the tranche application form on this listing.
This tranche application form will be visible to you after you have received your first tranche.
Both the photos from the event and scanned copies of the receipts are essential for processing your second tranche. Frequently Asked Questions Who is eligible to apply for event grants?
This program is currently in beta and only open for Superteam Members.
What criteria will the panelists use to evaluate grants?
We prefer to support members that have some prior experience in organizing events (regardless of how small) and events that are primarily focused on developers, artists, and investors.
Will I receive feedback on my proposal if it is rejected?
Unfortunately, our sponsors do not have the bandwidth to provide individualized feedback at this time.   Note: Getting approved for a grant is in no way to be understood as an endorsement or partnership.
Your event will be a community event, and in no way should you represent to third parties that it's a "Superteam event" or in any sense official.   Have a question that isn't answered here?  Email us at support@superteam.fun  for help.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: ZetaChain Ecosystem Grants is an ecosystem grant initiative powered by ZetaChain Ecosystem, designed to accelerate the development of critical protocols, developer tooling, and decentralized applications across ZetaChain Ecosystem ecosystem. The program provides milestone-based tranches sized according to project scope to empower talented engineering teams building scalable onchain solutions.

Grant capital is focused on high-priority infrastructure and use cases spanning DeFi, NFTs, Gaming, AI, helping teams move rapidly from prototype to production with direct technical and distribution support from ZetaChain Ecosystem.

Beyond capital, ZetaChain Ecosystem Grants connects recipients with core network engineers, security auditors, and community stakeholders to ensure smooth mainnet deployment and sustained user adoption.

sections.heading: Key focus areas & strategic priorities
paragraphs: The technical steering committee for ZetaChain Ecosystem Grants seeks proposals that deliver tangible utility and measurable onchain traction to ZetaChain Ecosystem ecosystem. Priority categories include:
bullets: Decentralized protocol engineering: Implementing secure smart contracts, state transition logic, and liquidity protocols tailored to ZetaChain Ecosystem ecosystem.
Developer frameworks & SDKs: Building open-source client libraries, testing suites, local testnets, and developer documentation that streamline onboarding.
Data availability & indexing infrastructure: Engineering high-throughput oracles, event indexers, and subgraphs for real-time protocol telemetry.
User-facing applications & interfaces: Launching accessible frontends, decentralized identity integrations, and automated agent workflows for global users.

sections.heading: Eligibility, evaluation & review criteria
paragraphs: Proposals for ZetaChain Ecosystem Grants are reviewed by core engineers and ecosystem evaluators using four primary criteria:
bullets: Architectural rigor and code quality: Well-structured GitHub repositories featuring clean commit histories, modular contracts, and comprehensive unit tests.
Clear ecosystem alignment: A focused value proposition that solves tangible technical bottlenecks or drives sustained transaction activity on ZetaChain Ecosystem ecosystem.
Team capability: Proven track record in software engineering, cryptography, or distributed systems capable of shipping complex deliverables on schedule.
Milestone feasibility: A well-defined work breakdown structure with concrete, verifiable acceptance criteria for each development sprint.

sections.heading: How to apply & milestone delivery
paragraphs: Founders and engineering teams can initiate their proposal via the official ZetaChain Ecosystem Grants portal at https://www.zetachain.com/blog/zetachain-grants-program-for-omnichain-dapp-builders. Submissions must include an architectural overview, link to public or private repositories, deliverable milestones, and budget allocation breakdown.

Applications are reviewed on a rolling intake cadence. Shortlisted teams participate in a technical discovery interview with ZetaChain Ecosystem's engineering committee to refine project milestones and security specifications.

Disbursements are milestone-gated: an initial tranche (25-30%) is provided upon onboarding, followed by milestone releases upon testnet deployment, successful smart contract audits, and production mainnet launch.

name: Zoho for Startups
description: While we intend to make this program available to all startups eventually, as of now, the program is exclusive for startups that are associated or incubated with our collaborators.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Zoho for Startups is an official founder perk and enablement program provided by Zoho, designed to assist early-stage software companies and engineering teams building modern technology products. Qualifying ventures receive up to Zoho One / apps credits in platform credits and operational resources, premium infrastructure access, and operational onboarding.

By eliminating upfront software costs across SaaS suite (Indian), the program enables startup teams to preserve runway while deploying robust, enterprise-ready infrastructure on Zoho's battle-tested platform.

Participating companies benefit from technical onboarding resources, direct guidance from Zoho's solutions engineering specialists, and structured pathways to scale as their commercial customer base expands.

sections.heading: Key focus areas & strategic priorities
paragraphs: The Zoho for Startups is tailored for ventures leveraging Zoho's platform to accelerate product delivery. Core focus areas include:
bullets: Production infrastructure deployment: Running mission-critical workloads, databases, and microservices on Zoho's cloud architecture.
Developer toolchain automation: Implementing CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, and developer environments using Zoho's developer platform.
Enterprise security and observability: Configuring end-to-end encryption, identity controls, and operational telemetry to meet industry compliance standards.
Scalable application architectures: Building and optimizing customer-facing web, mobile, and API-driven interfaces backed by Zoho's global network.

sections.heading: Eligibility, evaluation & review criteria
paragraphs: To qualify for Zoho for Startups, startup candidates must satisfy Zoho's standard program requirements:
bullets: Company stage and structure: Early-stage incorporated legal entity (typically Seed or Series A) with an active product domain and registered corporate identity.
Venture backing or affiliation: Participation in a recognized accelerator, venture fund portfolio, or startup partner network recognized by Zoho.
Product development readiness: A live product in development or production actively integrating Zoho's software tools into its technical stack.
Credit utilization history: First-time recipient status with no prior commercial redemptions of standard startup credits on Zoho's platform.

sections.heading: How to apply & milestone delivery
paragraphs: Eligible startups can apply directly on Zoho's program page at https://www.zoho.com/startups/. Complete the verification form with your company details, institutional email address, accelerator or investor affiliation, and technical stack summary.
Applications are evaluated on a rolling intake cadence. Decisions and credit provisioning are typically completed within 5 to 10 business days following account validation.
Once admitted, founders gain access to the developer console, onboarding workshops, and dedicated support channels to quickly integrate Zoho's tools into their infrastructure.
